body:
Update from @arybochkin's diff.

Schema table properties' field retain_delete_markers is not updated properly on index backfilling is done on tablet server side. This leads to using of HT<min> as a min time to check if tombstones should be removed from SST file. And as this is the min possible time, they are always kept in SST files during compaction and it's even not possible to remove them with manual compactions and with a help of tserver restart as the parameter retain_delete_markers is persisted as true and no other backfill done events can happen on an index table created and marked as backfilled.

The issue is a regression from 660e13af. On getting a backfill done event we were copying the current schema and were adding exactly one change: new_schema.SetRetainDeleteMarkers(false) and then metadata->SetSchema(new_schema). But the new schema was not applied as a subsequent call to TableInfo constructor with new_schema as an argument was ignoring a new schema as it has a requirement to have a different schema_version to make new schema be applied.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-8561](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-8561)
### Description

This issue tracks the fixup process for the indexes impacted by #19544. 

On tserver startup, the tserver identifies the set of indexes for which retain_delete_markers is set to true, checks with master if the index build is still in progress. If not, then the tserver can go ahead and fixup the local metadata - set retain_delete_markers to false and persist the changes locally (so that the subsequent restart no longer needs to perform the fixup again).

Scope the above change under a gflag(on by default), so as to have the ability to turn it off if necessary.

issue.title: [DocDB] Index tablets metadata backfilling state recovery at tserver

labels.name: kind/enhancement
labels.description: This is an enhancement of an existing feature

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-8565](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-8565)
### Description

As a continuation of https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/issues/19544, it is required to implement a mechanism to recover index tablets' metadata persisted with incorrect backfilling state.
The main idea is to setup a new RPC flow between tserver and master to be able to retrieve the actual backfilling state of index tables by tserver:
1) on ts_tablet_manager startup collect all existing index tablets with schema.table_properties.retain_delete_markers set to true in tablet metadata
2) prepare a set of index tables on base of the list of index tablets
3) issue RPC request from tserver to master with the set of index tables to check their actual backfilling state
4) check the actual backfilling status for those index tables at master
4) issue a RPC response from master to tserver with a set of index tables for which backfilling has been actually completed
5) update and flush metadata for the received index tables' tablets

issue.title: [DocDB] Backfill done may not be triggered for empty YCQL table

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-8884](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-8884)
### Description

This github tracks another case when indexes of empty YCQL tables have incorrect tablet metadata, leading to performance issues as described in #19544 

**Scenario**: `BackfillTable::AllowCompactionsToGCDeleteMarkers` is failing in case if index creation for the empty table.

**Steps to reproduce:**
```
1. create table tbl(k int primary key, v int) WITH transactions = { 'enabled' : true };
2. create index tbl_idx on tbl(v) WITH transactions = { 'enabled' : true };
```
The following log message can be observed:
```
E1106 13:32:57.176299 257064960 backfill_index.cc:1203] Index 76d2697586a04dd89d8f10bbd41ccdea is in state PREPARING : cannot enable compactions on it
```
And the subsequent `TabletServiceAdminImpl::BackfillDone()` is never triggered, which mean `retain_delete_markers` is never reset, which lead to the conditions described in https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/issues/19544.
Backfilling works fine if some data has been inserted:
```
create table tbl2(k int primary key, v int) WITH transactions = { 'enabled' : true };
insert into tbl2(k,v) values(1,1);
insert into tbl2(k,v) values(2,2);
insert into tbl2(k,v) values(3,3);
create index tbl2_idx on tbl2(v) WITH transactions = { 'enabled' : true };
```

**Note.** The side-effect of the issue is that `retain_delete_markers` is never reset in the sys catalog as the method [exits](https://github.com/yugabyte/yugabyte-db/blob/39b60d853006549f1391727000514a7e884ccad1/src/yb/master/backfill_index.cc#L1218) before changing the property.
